validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED, independent of GEM. This row is Line I ('первая нитка') of the Almaty-Bayserke-Talgar trunk gas pipeline, launched 28 October 2014 per the sheet's own existing ref, Tengrinews (verified live, 200 OK), which quotes the regional Akimat at the inauguration: pipeline 'has started working,' length 64.4 km, construction 'began in 2010,' cost '$428 million,' capacity '2.4 billion cubic meter per year,' built to serve 60 settlements / ~380,000 people. Independently corroborated as a real, currently-operating trunk system by: (1) Pipeline Technology Journal (2024), which describes 'the construction of a second gas pipeline between Almaty and Talgar, widely known as the Almaty-Baiserke-Talgar gas pipeline' -- language that presupposes a first/existing line, i.e. this row; (2) QazaqGaz's own Integrated Annual Report 2024 (igo_qazaqgaz_2024.pdf) -- the automated url_verifier FAILs on this PDF for Cyrillic tokens ('Интергаз'/'Байсерке'/'Талгар') even though the text is genuinely present (a known PDF-extraction limitation per the sweep's own guidance, not a dead/wrong source); I downloaded and read it directly with `pdftotext -layout` and confirmed the report lists 'МГ «Алматы – Байсерке – Талгар»' among Intergas Central Asia's ten trunk-pipeline production-management assets (p.1253 of the extracted text), and separately covers the SECOND line's Dec-2024 in-service milestone (p.1282/6794) -- i.e. the report itself treats the two lines as distinct, confirming both are real and this row is not a phantom or a re-record of the other.

CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED as transmission. The Russian designation 'магистральный газопровод' (МГ) = trunk/transmission-grade pipeline, and this line sits in Intergas Central Asia's trunk (transmission) portfolio -- the national trunk operator, not a local gas-distribution utility -- despite ultimately feeding many small settlements; local distribution networks branch off this trunk line, they are not this line. Fuel=Gas is trivially correct.

DUPLICATE (orchestrator's structural lead re: P6831, RESOLVED -- NOT a duplicate): P6830 and P6831 are two genuinely separate, physically distinct parallel pipelines under one corridor name, built a decade apart. P6830 (this row, SegmentName 'I'): built 2010-2014, 64.4 km, cap 2.4 bcm/y, diameter not stated in any source found -- confirmed above. P6831 ('Line II'): built October 2023-December 2024 (in-service 19.12.2024 per QazaqGaz IGO 2024 p.1282; intergas.kz's own May-2024 construction update at https://intergas.kz/ru/news/4/1040 gives the SAME 62.4 km / 530 mm and reports work running ahead of schedule), capacity stated in the IGO report as 1,000,000 nm3/hr = ~8.76 bcm/y (matches GEM's 8.8 for P6831 within rounding), cost 31.8 bn tenge -- an entirely separate, later capital project explicitly built to supply gas conversion of Almaty's thermal power plants (a presidential directive). Pipeline Technology Journal frames it as 'a second gas pipeline' i.e. an ADDITION alongside the first, never a replacement or a re-record of it. No merge recommended; both rows are legitimate and already correctly distinguished by SegmentName ('I' here).
